evidence.exact_quote: - Editing Deep Plan markdown updates the normalized TODO projection before execution begins.

items.impact: Concurrent markdown edits, auto-use proposals, and status mutations can race or overwrite one another because no revision token, compare-and-swap rule, or conflict outcome is defined.
items.statement: TODO mutation and review ordering are explicit, but the contract does not define atomic synchronization when multiple mutation sources revise the projection before execution.
items.title: TODO resynchronization lacks a concurrency contract

evidence.exact_quote: - Mutating annotations are applied only through targeted revision after validation.

items.impact: The explicit boundary prevents direct annotation-driven patch application and keeps visible review separate from durable mutation.
items.statement: Standard and Deep Plan review surfaces retain a clear user-review boundary: annotation actions are source-backed, visible, and mutation-capable only through validated targeted revision.
items.title: Plan review and annotation mutation boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - Interrupted revision runs preserve revision_id and resume lineage.

items.impact: A resumed revision can duplicate changes, apply against a newer document, or leave mixed annotation states without an idempotency key, document-version precondition, commit boundary, or rollback rule.
items.statement: Revision lineage, reanchoring, and visible composer handoff are specified, but interrupted targeted revision lacks atomic resume and conflict semantics.
items.title: Targeted revision recovery is not atomic or idempotent

evidence.exact_quote: - If another run is active in the same thread, accepted execution may queue behind it through Queue Execution.

items.impact: Users and runtimes cannot determine whether repeated acceptance deduplicates, how queued plans are ordered or cancelled, or which frozen artifact executes if the thread changes meanwhile.
items.statement: Selection privacy, four-way approval, frozen execution handoff, and wizard escalation are bounded, but Queue Execution has no ordering, deduplication, cancellation, or stale-artifact contract.
items.title: Accepted-plan queue behavior is underspecified

evidence.exact_quote: - Multi-file turn reverts apply to the whole turn across affected files.

items.impact: A failure after restoring only some files could corrupt the worktree while the UI reports a whole-turn revert; no preflight, transaction, compensating rollback, or partial-failure state is defined.
items.statement: Visible file references are safely bounded, but the destructive whole-turn multi-file revert requires atomicity and recovery semantics that are absent.
items.title: Whole-turn multi-file revert lacks partial-failure safety

evidence.exact_quote: - Chat does not own hunk-level stage, unstage, discard, conflict-review, or commit operations.

items.impact: The boundary prevents Assistant Chat projections from becoming a second source-control authority.
items.statement: Chat is explicitly a review consumer that deep-links to canonical SCM owners; aggregate files-touched and worktree cards do not own SCM truth.
items.title: Source-control ownership remains outside chat

evidence.exact_quote: - Assistant, Interview, and subagents can retrieve relevant prior messages or sessions when answering or planning.

items.impact: Human and agent chat-history retrieval are provided without transferring project-wide find/replace or symbol-search ownership into chat.
items.statement: The plan defines distinct human and agent chat-history search consumers while preserving Search side-panel and editor/LSP ownership boundaries.
items.title: Chat-history search has explicit consumers and owner boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: - Per-source query, hit, and byte caps prevent retrieved context from crowding out user/assistant messages.

items.impact: Builders can choose incompatible caps and trigger thresholds, and tests cannot prove bounded context pressure or predictable latency without normative values or a deterministic derivation algorithm.
items.statement: Project-only retrieval scope, settings, and memory separation are explicit, but deterministic per-source budgets and trigger heuristics have no normative values or derivation contract.
items.title: Auto-retrieval budgets are named but not measurable

evidence.exact_quote: - logread payloads are bounded by size caps and stricter permission defaults.

items.impact: Without schemas for result ordering, pagination, truncation markers, authorization failures, and cap values, tool callers cannot reliably distinguish complete, truncated, denied, or stale results.
items.statement: Agent search tool signatures are listed, but their result and failure contracts remain incomplete, including the bounded logread behavior called out by acceptance criteria.
items.title: Agent search result and failure schemas are incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: - Missing, disabled, corrupted, building, invalid, or query-skipped indices fall back to raw ripgrep.

items.impact: Fallback could bypass index-level exclusions or permissions, expose files unexpectedly, hang on large repositories, or provide no cancellation/progress signal.
items.statement: Raw-ripgrep fallback and per-project index partitioning are explicit, but permission parity, cancellation, progress, and worst-case scale behavior for fallback are not.
items.title: Search fallback lacks permission and scale guarantees

evidence.exact_quote: - Rendering vocabulary is not extended outside the closed taxonomy without a later SSOT contract.

items.impact: Persisted message_type values provide a falsifiable restore, export, search, and rendering contract instead of relying on presentation inference.
items.statement: Thread-management scope correctly delegates concrete behavior, and the closed message taxonomy is persisted independently of lifecycle and runtime presentation.
items.title: Message taxonomy and persistence boundary are closed

evidence.exact_quote: - Deletion removes the thread from normal user-visible chat surfaces while retaining only required integrity, sync, or compliance metadata.

items.impact: Implementations cannot determine which records survive deletion, for how long, under whose authority, or how privacy erasure and sync tombstones interact.
items.statement: Lifecycle separation and stable identity are defined, but deletion retention is left as an open-ended integrity, sync, or compliance exception without a data-lifecycle contract.
items.title: Thread deletion has no bounded retention contract

evidence.exact_quote: - A materially different debug target requires an explicit supersede action.

items.impact: Two callers can both observe no active mutation-capable investigation and start competing work, or supersede against stale state, unless an atomic claim/version rule exists.
items.statement: Terminal-thread compatibility and explicit supersession are clear, but the one-active-investigation invariant lacks an atomic acquisition and stale-supersede contract.
items.title: Single active debug investigation is not race-safe

evidence.exact_quote: - New mutation-capable debugging against the same target waits until residue is handled.

items.impact: Unsafe residue may be cleared inconsistently because the plan does not name who may declare resolved, rolled back, or promoted, nor the evidence required to unblock mutation.
items.statement: Restore and cleanup prevent silent target rebinding, but clearance from failed_cleanup has no explicit authority, proof, or auditable transition oracle.
items.title: Failed-cleanup clearance lacks authority and evidence

evidence.exact_quote: - Initial browser/evidence and cleanup/resume ceilings are enforced as machine-readable values.

items.impact: The runtime lacks a defined response when fixed ceilings are exhausted and no authorized override path is stated; route_target failures likewise have no fallback or recovery result here.
items.statement: Machine-readable stop codes, debug ceilings, and shared route ownership are present, but ceiling exhaustion authority and route-resolution failure behavior are incomplete.
items.title: Debug ceilings and navigation failures lack recovery policy

evidence.exact_quote: - Branching from running or dirty threads requires explicit confirmation naming source state and branch target.

items.impact: The thread, worktree, or runtime identity can change after confirmation but before branch creation, making the confirmation label stale and potentially branching an unintended state.
items.statement: Frozen runtime display, branch lineage, confirmation, and inactive-thread attention are specified, but branch creation lacks a version precondition tying confirmation to the committed source state.
items.title: Branch confirmation is vulnerable to state drift

evidence.exact_quote: - Side-panel, artifact-local, and chat-local usage route wording remains stale/non-buildable until reconciled.

items.impact: Consumers cannot safely build context-usage navigation until all owner documents and command routes converge on the editor-tab Context Detail Pane.
items.statement: The plan explicitly marks competing side-panel, artifact-local, and chat-local context-usage routes as stale and non-buildable pending cross-document reconciliation.
items.title: Context-usage routing is explicitly non-buildable

evidence.exact_quote: - Raw exposes payloads, tool-part data, provider metadata, and runtime/path debug data.

items.impact: Raw provider/tool payloads may contain secrets, malicious markup, local paths, or oversized content; absent access, redaction, escaping, and bounded-render rules create disclosure and UI-safety risks.
items.statement: The Context Detail Pane information architecture is clear, but Raw view lacks explicit authorization, redaction, untrusted-content rendering, size, and accessibility contracts.
items.title: Raw Context Detail Pane lacks security and rendering boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: - Omitted context is never presented as serialized.

items.impact: The explicit distinction prevents the UI from overstating what the model received and forbids a second chat-local cost model.
items.statement: Canonical runtime usage, visible serialization state, bounded Investigation Context, and canonical header-field consumption establish a strong truth boundary.
items.title: Usage and Investigation Context truth are explicitly bounded

evidence.exact_quote: - Only active and redacted items serialize into prompt context.

items.impact: A redacted item could still leak sensitive raw text, refs, metadata, or recoverable identifiers because the required serialized representation and noninterference oracle are undefined.
items.statement: Item-state eligibility and visible auto-ingestion are clear, but permitting redacted items to serialize requires a precise safe representation and leakage test that are absent.
items.title: Redacted prompt serialization has no leakage oracle

evidence.exact_quote: - Revocation does not delete the underlying artifact record.

items.impact: Users may reasonably interpret revoke as removal while sensitive raw artifacts persist indefinitely; the plan does not define retention, deletion authority, UI disclosure, or failures for revoke/export/revalidate actions.
items.statement: Artifact ownership and bounded references are explicit, but revocation deliberately preserves raw records without a corresponding retention, deletion, authorization, and user-disclosure contract.
items.title: Investigation artifact revocation is not deletion-safe

evidence.exact_quote: - Operation-card content is read-only and non-interactive.

items.impact: Concurrent commands and retries can reorder or duplicate cards, associate updates with the wrong card, or lose correlation to terminal and diff details without stable instance and attempt rules.
items.statement: Shared card ownership, bounded read-only previews, and subtype actions are well bounded, but command-instance correlation, retry lineage, and out-of-order update handling are not defined.
items.title: Operation-card instance and retry correlation are missing

evidence.exact_quote: - Completed results plus failure detail are returned.

items.impact: Builders cannot determine all legal card transitions, terminal-state update rejection, sibling cancellation, side-effect rollback, or how partial results map to card and task failure states.
items.statement: The card state list, widget exclusions, and stop-on-first-failure default are explicit, but the complete transition table and side-effect semantics for partial batch failure are absent.
items.title: Operation state machine and batch partial failure are incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: - The four-tier approval ladder remains visible and machine-readable.

items.impact: An always grant may outlive the intended account, project, tool, or resource scope, and terminal retries may orphan prior sessions because revocation propagation and old-terminal cleanup are not specified.
items.statement: Visible permission status and terminal handoff ownership are defined, but persistent grant scope/revocation and retry cleanup for old terminal sessions remain unsafe negative space.
items.title: Persistent approvals and terminal retries lack lifecycle safety

segments.summary: Reviewed TODO mutation, plan review, annotation lifecycle, recovery, and visible selection handoff; found concurrency and revision atomicity gaps while confirming the direct-mutation boundary.
Reviewed target privacy, post-plan approval and execution, wizard escalation, file references, revert, and SCM projections; found queue and destructive partial-failure gaps.
Reviewed chat and agent search ownership, project-only retrieval, budgets, settings, memory boundary, and search tools; found non-measurable budgets and incomplete result contracts.
Reviewed search freshness/fallback, GUI logs, index partitioning, message taxonomy, rendering persistence, and thread lifecycle; found fallback parity and deletion-retention gaps.
Reviewed terminal-thread compatibility, debug investigation lifecycle, restore, cleanup, stop reasons, budgets, and shared navigation; found race, cleanup authority, and recovery-policy gaps.
Reviewed runtime snapshots, branching, thread focus, context usage ownership/routes/signals, and Context Detail Pane IA; found state-drift, explicit non-buildability, and Raw-view security gaps.
Reviewed canonical usage truth and Investigation Context scope, fields, item states, ingestion, artifact ownership, and rendering; found redaction-leakage and revocation-retention gaps.

Reviewed operation-card ownership, anatomy, subtypes, state machine, exclusions, batch semantics, permission status, and terminal handoff; found correlation, partial-failure, approval-scope, and cleanup gaps.

cross_document_questions: Which owner contract resolves all context-usage opens to the editor-tab Context Detail Pane and retires side-panel, artifact-local, and chat-local routes?
Which storage and privacy owner defines deletion, revocation, redaction, and compliance-retention semantics for threads and Investigation Context artifacts?
Which runtime contract owns atomic multi-file revert, targeted-revision resume, execution queue ordering, and terminal retry cleanup?
Which permission contract defines the scope, persistence, revocation propagation, and account/project binding of always approvals?
